title: User Signal Dies at the Retrieval Boundary - Sonam Pankaj, StarlightSearch
talk_summary: The talk pitches a runtime memory layer that retrieves past experiences weighted by whether they helped or hurt task outcomes, then promotes repeated lessons into skills. It offers a useful loop from traces/evals to retrieval, but the evidence is vendor benchmarks and a demo, with cold-start and noisy-label caveats.

takeaways.what_they_do: Store past run experiences and retrieve them by semantic similarity to the current task, re-ranked by whether those memories historically helped or hurt execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: retrieve by semantic similarity to the current task weighted by whether those memories have historically helped or hurt

takeaways.what_they_do: Consume observability traces and eval pass/fail signals, then convert them into retrieval guidance for future agent runs instead of leaving them in dashboards.
takeaways.evidence_quote: system that consume traces, absorb eval, and convert both into retrieval guidance for future runs

takeaways.what_they_do: After enough accumulated memories, bake the recurring reasoning into a skill so the agent stays updated without editing the base prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we bake in the reasoning and the understanding into skills so that your agent always remains updated

takeaways.what_they_do: Store task-useful reasoning and action guidance with context/history, rather than static user facts or preferences.
takeaways.evidence_quote: treat memory as reasoning, not as facts

takeaways.what_they_do: Feed past review/execution outcomes back into retrieval re-ranking so similar future tasks retrieve lessons that actually caught or missed defects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: event outcome becomes a first-class signal in the retrieval re-ranking

takeaways.what_they_do: Avoid stuffing all history into context; retrieve only a small set of high-utility memories ranked by past usefulness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of the agents deal with context stuffing
